messages:
support-l1: FYI customer ACME reported a sudden latency spike + 5xx/queue responses starting ~1719865390. They say they pinned eu-west1 but responses show x-served-region: us-east1 and a billing spike. Any incident?

sre-jordan: Can you paste one of the failing response headers and a sample request id?

support-l1: request_id 01G8X2Y7, sample curl: ```curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -H "x-region: eu-west1" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"test"}'``` Response headers: `x-served-region: us-east1`, `x-fallback-reason: capacity_exhausted`, body had `error: queued, now_fallback`.

infra-bot: [autoscaler] eu-west1-dedicated pool scale attempt at 1719865420: desired=12, current=12, hard_limit=12 -> cannot scale (quota). Fallback policy=spill_to_hosted_by_region_priority.

eng-platform-lee: Noted. Sounds like dedicated eu-west1 hit its hard cap and the routing policy allowed spillover to other regions (us-east1). That explains cross-region latency and extra billing.

alice-prod: Do we know if the customer explicitly requested dedicated eu-west1 or are they on hosted with region preference? customer plan?

support-l1: ACME is on Dedicated Reserved (monthly commit). They set `region_pin: eu-west1` in console but our routing still spilled. They expected request to queue or error, not be served from another region.

sre-jordan: Root cause hypothesis: pool reached hard_limit -> autoscaler couldn't provision (quota/placement) -> router honored fallback_policy=allow_spill -> spilled to hosted pool in us-east1 (cheaper/available) -> cost & latency. We should check the per-customer fallback override flags.

eng-platform-lee: Repro steps I used locally: 1) create traffic hitting eu-west1 dedicated until pool hits limit (abbreviated). 2) router logs show: `router: route_attempt {region=eu-west1, pool=dedicated, result=capacity_exhausted, action=spill->us-east1}` 3) response sent with `x-fallback-region: us-east1`.

support-ops: Customer wants immediate mitigation and a clear explanation. They don't want cross-region serving for compliance. Can we roll back spillover for their account and drain existing cross-region requests?

sre-jordan: Yes. Immediate options: (A) set account-level routing_override: `spill_policy: reject_on_capacity_exhaustion` so requests return 503 instead of spilling; (B) temporarily create emergency dedicated capacity in eu-west1 (manual allocation) and bind to account; (C) update routing table to prefer eu-central1 as second-choice instead of us-east1 (lower latency). I can apply A and C now.

eng-platform-lee: To apply A for account acme-corp: `POST /admin/accounts/acme-corp/routing {"spill_policy":"reject"}` (requires infra-admin). To change second-choice runbook: update region_priority for account. Note: rejecting will surface errors to customer — make them aware.

support-l1: Please do A + C. Also need copy for the customer explaining what happened and recommended long-term fixes.

infra-bot: action: created ticket INFRA-3921 for manual allocation request. autoscaler note: quota request needed for eu-west1 GPUs.

sre-jordan: Applied routing_override for acme-corp -> spill_policy=reject at 1719865720. Also updated account region_priority to [eu-west1, eu-central1] (no us-east1) at 1719865760.

support-ops: Confirmed with ACME: after change they saw their next requests return 503 when eu-west1 is full, instead of being served cross-region. They are happy for now but want capacity fix.

alice-prod: For customer-facing note: short summary — dedicated pool in eu-west1 hit committed hard limit; autoscaler couldn't add nodes (quota/placement); router fallback allowed spill to hosted us-east1 causing latency and extra charges. Immediate fix: disabled spillover for ACME and set eu-central1 as fallback. Next steps: work with sales/infra to expand reserved capacity or request quota increase.

eng-platform-lee: Long-term options to present: - increase reserved GPUs for Dedicated contract - add soft-queueing behavior that buffers short bursts instead of immediate spill - provide explicit account-level fallback controls in Console (UI flag) — tracking ticket PRODX-1145.

support-l1: Customer thanked us and asked for ETA on quota increase. Who owns quota request with cloud?

sre-jordan: Infra owns; I filed quota request with cloud provider (ticket CP-77891). Estimated response 24-72h. In parallel we can provision temporary spare nodes from warm pool if infra approves.

support-ops: Customer accepted temporary 503 behavior for now. We'll follow up with weekly progress updates.

support-l1: Closing loop: ACME confirmed reduced latency/billing after changes. Will update ticket and follow up on quota. :white_check_mark:
